about: Made by tools/browser_support_table.mjs from MDN's browser-compat-data; read by tests/browser-support.test.mjs. Do not edit the numbers: run the tool again. The notes in "features" (how, fallback) are written by a person and kept.

css-at:page.fallback: Print only: the paper margins. An older browser prints with its own margins.

css-at:property.fallback: Registered custom properties only let the sky colours fade between seasons. An older browser changes them at once (the colours are the same).

css-gap:flex.fallback: Chrome before 84 and Safari before 14.1 (iPhone before iOS 14.5) put no space between the items of a flex box (buttons, chips, cards in a row touch). Everything still reads and works. Counted as flex when the rule does not say grid.

css-media:forced-colors.fallback: Windows high-contrast colours; an older browser leaves the colours as they are (and Firefox before 89 / Chrome before 89 have no high-contrast mode to adapt to).

css-media:prefers-contrast.fallback: A little more contrast for people who ask for it; others see the normal look.

css-media:prefers-reduced-transparency.fallback: A solid header for people who ask for less see-through; others see the normal look.

css-media:scripting.fallback: Hides the things that need a script when scripts are off. A browser that does not know it also gets the .no-js class from js/guard.js, so nothing is lost.

css-prop:-webkit-backdrop-filter.fallback: Safari wrote it with -webkit- until 18; both are written. Firefox before 103 shows the header without the blur (its colour is already 94% solid).

css-prop:-webkit-tap-highlight-color.fallback: Removes the grey flash when a finger taps a button on iPhone and Android. Other browsers have no such flash.

css-prop:-webkit-text-size-adjust.fallback: Stops Safari on a phone making text bigger when the phone is turned sideways. Other browsers do not do that.

css-prop:-webkit-touch-callout.fallback: Stops the iPhone pop-up menu on a long press of the farm drawings. Other browsers have none.

css-prop:accent-color.fallback: The tick boxes of the checklist keep the browser's own colour.

css-prop:ascent-override.fallback: Metrics of the stand-in font (see the comment in css/styles.css). Without them the text can move a little when the real font arrives.

css-prop:aspect-ratio.fallback: The season cards and the photo boxes get their height from it. Without it the season cards (drawings laid on top with position:absolute) would be 0 high, so css/styles.css has "@supports not (aspect-ratio:1)" that gives them a block of the right height. Other uses only crop pictures to a shape or round the week circles; an older browser shows the pictures in their own shape and the week circles as pills. The farm map's box gets one from a script (js/features.js) only to hold its place while the map loads; without it the box has no reserved height until the map is drawn.

css-prop:backdrop-filter.fallback: Written together with the -webkit- one. A browser without it shows the header without the blur (its colour is already 94% solid).

css-prop:border-block.fallback: The same sides are written the old way (top/right/bottom/left, padding-top ..., margin-left ...) just before it, so Chrome before 87 and Safari before 14.1 read those. The page is left to right in every language.

css-prop:box-decoration-break.fallback: Print only: where a long heading breaks across two pages.

css-prop:color-scheme.fallback: "only light" tells browsers not to darken the site by themselves. A browser that does not know it has no such automatic dark mode (Chrome before 81, Firefox before 96).

css-prop:container-type.fallback: Only for the progress tractor and vine in the page margin, which are measured against their box. css/styles.css has "@supports not (width:1cqw)" that places them with left: instead.

css-prop:content-visibility.fallback: Lets a browser skip drawing the closed FAQ answers; others draw them.

css-prop:font-synthesis.fallback: Stops a browser inventing a bold Chinese or Hindi face; an older one may.

css-prop:forced-color-adjust.fallback: Keeps the selected tab visible in high-contrast mode; where unknown the browser picks its own colours.

css-prop:inset.fallback: The same sides are written the old way (top/right/bottom/left, padding-top ..., margin-left ...) just before it, so Chrome before 87 and Safari before 14.1 read those. The page is left to right in every language.

css-prop:margin-block.fallback: The same sides are written the old way (top/right/bottom/left, padding-top ..., margin-left ...) just before it, so Chrome before 87 and Safari before 14.1 read those. The page is left to right in every language.

css-prop:margin-inline.fallback: The same sides are written the old way (top/right/bottom/left, padding-top ..., margin-left ...) just before it, so Chrome before 87 and Safari before 14.1 read those. The page is left to right in every language.

css-prop:overscroll-behavior.fallback: Keeps a scroll in the photo viewer from scrolling the page behind it (Safari before 16 lets it).

css-prop:padding-block.fallback: The same sides are written the old way (top/right/bottom/left, padding-top ..., margin-left ...) just before it, so Chrome before 87 and Safari before 14.1 read those. The page is left to right in every language.

css-prop:padding-inline.fallback: The same sides are written the old way (top/right/bottom/left, padding-top ..., margin-left ...) just before it, so Chrome before 87 and Safari before 14.1 read those. The page is left to right in every language.

css-prop:rotate.fallback: Single-property transforms (rotate, scale, translate) arrived in Chrome 104 and Safari 14.1. They are the little tilts of the photos, the hover pops, the spinning sun rays, the falling leaves and snow, and the position of the progress tractor. An older browser shows the photos straight, no pop, and leaves and snow that fade but do not fall. The tractor is placed with left: instead wherever container units are missing (see container-type), and every browser that has container units has translate.

css-prop:scroll-behavior.fallback: Anchor links jump instead of gliding (Safari before 15.4).

css-prop:scroll-margin-top.fallback: Where an anchor link stops under the sticky header; Safari before 14.1 stops a little too high.

css-prop:scrollbar-gutter.fallback: Keeps the page from shifting when the photo viewer hides the scroll bar; an older browser shifts a few pixels.

css-prop:size.fallback: The paper size of the printed pages (@page); an older browser uses its own.

css-prop:text-decoration-thickness.fallback: A thicker link underline; an older browser draws the normal one.

css-prop:text-underline-offset.fallback: A lower underline; an older browser draws the normal one.

css-prop:text-wrap.fallback: Balanced line breaks in headings and buttons; an older browser breaks them the old way.

css-prop:user-select.fallback: Written with -webkit-user-select next to it (Safari needs that one).

css-pseudo:backdrop.fallback: The dark cloth behind the photo viewer. A browser without <dialog> never gets it, and js/main.js draws its own box-shadow cloth then (the .lb-fallback rule in css/styles.css).

css-pseudo:details-content.fallback: Animates the FAQ answers opening; an older browser opens them at once.

css-pseudo:focus-visible.fallback: A browser that does not know :focus-visible (Safari before 15.4, Firefox before 85, Chrome before 86) drops those rules, and the browser's own focus ring is still there: nothing in the site switches the ring off for :focus (only #main, which a script focuses, and rules that sit inside :focus-visible themselves). The yellow or white extra rings are lost. Rules written in a list with other selectors are lost together.

css-pseudo:has.fallback: A browser without :has() (Safari before 15.4, Chrome before 105, Firefox before 121) drops the rule. Each use was read: the empty live badge box is shown empty, five photos stay in a row, the checklist has a :checked + * rule for the strike-through, the focus ring on a chip or photo has an @supports selector(:has(*)) fallback, the page behind the photo viewer can scroll, and a focused reveal block is revealed when it scrolls into view anyway. One use has no fallback: without it the message in the hero picker card does not leave room for the round Pause animations button in its corner, so the first line can run under that button.

css-pseudo:is.fallback: A rule with :is() is dropped whole by Chrome before 88 and Samsung Internet 13 to 14. These are: the Spanish and Vietnamese menu for windows between 1180 and 1330 pixels wide, line heights for Hindi, Chinese and Vietnamese, the 44-pixel touch area around buttons, a few tweaks for very small or very short screens, the printed page, and what shows when scripts fail. Reading and every button work without them.

css-unit:cqh.fallback: See container-type. (The vertical track on a small screen is decoration.)

css-unit:dvh.fallback: Only inside @supports (height:1dvh), after the same rule in vh.

css-unit:svh.fallback: Written after the same property in vh, so a browser without svh keeps the vh line.

css-value:backdrop-filter:none.fallback: Switches the blur off where it is not wanted; a browser with no blur has nothing to switch off.

css-value:border-block:solid.fallback: The same sides are written the old way (top/right/bottom/left, padding-top ..., margin-left ...) just before it, so Chrome before 87 and Safari before 14.1 read those. The page is left to right in every language.

css-value:cursor:not-allowed.fallback: A mouse pointer shape. Phones have no pointer.

css-value:cursor:pointer.fallback: A mouse pointer shape. Phones have no pointer.

css-value:cursor:zoom-in.fallback: A mouse pointer shape. Phones have no pointer.

css-value:inset:auto.fallback: The same sides are written the old way (top/right/bottom/left, padding-top ..., margin-left ...) just before it, so Chrome before 87 and Safari before 14.1 read those. The page is left to right in every language.

css-value:margin-inline:auto.fallback: The same sides are written the old way (top/right/bottom/left, padding-top ..., margin-left ...) just before it, so Chrome before 87 and Safari before 14.1 read those. The page is left to right in every language.

css-value:overflow-wrap:anywhere.fallback: overflow-wrap:break-word is written just before it (Safari before 15.4 does not know "anywhere").

css-value:overflow-x:clip.fallback: css/styles.css has "@supports not (overflow-x:clip)" that uses overflow-x:hidden on the same elements.

css-value:touch-action:pinch-zoom.fallback: Keeps pinch-zoom working on the drawings in Firefox 85 and later; before that the value is ignored and the browser decides.

css-value:width:fit-content.fallback: width:-moz-fit-content is written just before it (Firefox before 94).

html-attr:details.name.fallback: Makes the FAQ questions close each other; an older browser lets several stay open.

html-attr:img.loading.fallback: Lazy loading; an older browser loads the picture at once.

html-attr:input.inputmode.fallback: The keyboard hint for the e-mail box (Firefox before 95 ignores it; type="email" gives the same keyboard).

html-attr:link.fetchpriority.fallback: A hint on the font preload line: a browser without it still preloads the font, only without the priority hint (the page loads a little later, nothing is missing).

html-el:dialog.fallback: The photo viewer. js/main.js tests typeof HTMLDialogElement and its showModal before using it and otherwise draws the same box as a plain fixed box (.lb-fallback in css/styles.css).

html-rel:manifest.fallback: Add to Home Screen for Safari 17; before that the site is just a bookmark.

html-rel:preload.fallback: Starts the fonts a little sooner; Firefox before 85 finds them when the style sheet asks.

js-name:at.fallback: The site's own property (the moment a pizza release opens, the number of medals for an achievement) and a function in js/main.js. Never Array.at() (Safari before 15.4, Chrome before 92).

js-name:close.fallback: Mostly the site's own names (the closing time of the opening hours, the function that closes the notice or a medal). The one real <dialog>.close() in js/main.js runs only when typeof HTMLDialogElement says there is a <dialog>.

js-name:doNotTrack.fallback: Only read to see whether a visitor asked not to be counted; where it is missing the answer is "no request" and the other spellings are read too.

js-name:getAnimations.fallback: Tested with typeof before use, and the other call is inside try.

js-name:hasOwn.fallback: The site's own helper in js/i18n.js, written with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call. Not Object.hasOwn() (Safari before 15.4, Chrome before 93).

js-name:loading.fallback: The loading attribute of a picture; an older browser ignores it.

js-name:requestIdleCallback.fallback: Safari does not have it at all. Both scripts test for it and use setTimeout instead.

js-name:show.fallback: The site's own function (show the drive time answer). Not <dialog>.show().

js-name:showModal.fallback: Used only after the typeof test of HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal.

js-name:visualViewport.fallback: Every use starts with a test of window.visualViewport.

unresolved.css-fn:format: The format("woff2") hint of @font-face; every target reads woff2.
unresolved.css-prop:-webkit-font-smoothing: A Mac and iPhone only text smoothing setting; others ignore it.
unresolved.css-pseudo:-webkit-details-marker: Hides the old Safari triangle on <summary>; other browsers ignore the rule.
unresolved.html-attr:button.role: ARIA role attribute (not in the compat data).
unresolved.html-attr:div.role: ARIA role attribute (not in the compat data).
unresolved.html-attr:input.type: The type of an input; the values are checked one by one (html-input).
unresolved.html-attr:input.value: A plain attribute of old HTML.
unresolved.html-attr:meta.property: Open Graph tags; read by link previews, not by browsers.
unresolved.html-attr:p.role: ARIA role attribute (not in the compat data).
unresolved.html-attr:table.role: ARIA role attribute (not in the compat data).
unresolved.html-attr:tbody.role: ARIA role attribute (not in the compat data).
unresolved.html-attr:th.role: ARIA role attribute (not in the compat data).
unresolved.html-attr:thead.role: ARIA role attribute (not in the compat data).
unresolved.html-attr:tr.role: ARIA role attribute (not in the compat data).
unresolved.html-el:wa-en: The site's own tag for a name that stays in English; a browser that does not know a tag shows it as plain inline text.
unresolved.html-rel:apple-touch-icon: The iPhone home screen icon (old, only Safari reads it).
unresolved.svg-attr:svg.focusable: Old Internet Explorer / Edge attribute; others ignore it.
unresolved.svg-attr:svg.hidden: The global hidden attribute on an svg.
